newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia commercial property to firm - NAB.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia commercial property to firm - NAB.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) on Thursday forecast firmer yields and values in the Australian commercial property market in the year to June 30, 1997.

"Our reading of the market suggests some further firming in yields and values over the present financial year as end user demand picks up," NAB managing director Don Argus told a Property Council of Australia luncheon.
Argus noted that the office sector was showing improved rent and vacancies which he expected to be reflected in a gradual improvement in capital values.
"Most of the activity remains centred in Sydney and secondary office markets everywhere remain oversupplied," he added.
Rents in the industrial property market were likely to plateau while capital value was seen stable to likely lower, Argus said.
Hospitality sector room rates were moving higher and new development proposals were emerging, he said.
"In this sector capital values are likely to remain very site and project specific, and we hesistate to project an overall trend," Argus said.
The current overhang of residential housing stock was seen gradually unwinding during 1996/97 followed by a modest upswing in new dwelling constructions.
"Overall we still expect dwelling construction to make a negative contribution to growth in the current year," he said.

Across most property sectors, the bank saw the market's primamry influence as low inflation coupled with moderate economic growth with the exception of activity surrounding the 2000 Olympic Games in Sydney.
